cells.ranking_metric: Debian popcon installations of the lead's runtime library binary package (max when two sonames are listed)
cells.selection: expat (libexpat1 297,134) and libxml2 (libxml2 binary 290,724) are the two format-aware C XML parsers with the highest Debian popcon counts; mxml (libmxml1 2,054) is third and the only other lead with a primary value. All three are verified. Homebrew 365-day installs give the same order (expat 1,360,500, libxml2 564,778, libmxml 127).
cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell: three third-party paths (expat 2.10.0, libxml2 2.15.4 and Mini-XML 4.0.6) were built, matched the exact namespace-resolved summary of both valid controls under LLVM source coverage, and have native AFL++ feedback with a stable valid-control differential. They are three distinct parser families. expat leads libxml2 by 6,410 installs (2.2%) on the binary-package metric, a near tie; mxml is two orders of magnitude lower (2,054, 1,842 of them in popcon's no-files column). The Debian sourcemax table would invert the first two (libxml2 source 61,109) only because the libxml2 source now builds libxml2-16 and the older libxml2 binary is no longer attributed to it, so binary runtime-library counts are the primary metric; libxml2-16 (9,413) is not added because hosts may have both. mxml's value is the 3.x soname libmxml1; the pinned 4.0.6 is Debian forky/sid's mxml source, and its libmxml4 binary has no row in the saved snapshot. Mini-XML does not implement Namespaces in XML: it returns prefix:local names and keeps xmlns declarations as attributes, so its expanded names, declaration counts and URIs are computed by the adapter from mxml's tree, not by the package. Popcon counts installations, mostly pulled in as dependencies, not direct parser use. Search was the Conan Center recipe-name substring 'xml' (9 hits, 1 of them a C XML parser) plus seven targeted C names; Conan and Debian miss vendored single-file parsers. The control oracle (controls/xml/check_controls.py) uses Python's pyexpat, the same family as expat but not libxml2 or Mini-XML, so those matches are cross-family checks. The expat harness pins XML_SetHashSalt so AFL++ maps are reproducible; libxml2 and mxml needed no such change. ISO C documents no XML API. Two valid UTF-8 controls without DOCTYPE do not establish DTD, entity, encoding, XML 1.1 or rejection behaviour.

cells.selection: mpg123 has the highest Homebrew install-on-request count (12,256) among hits whose own C library decodes MPEG Layer III frames from a documented byte API. lame (6,992) ranks next but its HIP decoder is built over libmpg123. mad (libmad 0.16.5, 1,145) is the next independent decoder family and is verified through mad_stream_buffer/mad_frame_decode/mad_synth_frame.
cells.uncertainty: Two verified paths from two independent decoder families; no lower-ranked filler entries. Search is a substring match over all Homebrew formula names and descriptions for seven queries, captured 2026-11-17; it misses header-only decoders that are not packaged there. minimp3 and dr_mp3 have no value on the primary metric, so their GitHub stars are recorded as supplemental only and are not compared with Homebrew counts. libmad needs MAD_BUFFER_GUARD (8) zero bytes appended after the input; the harness adds exactly that and counts every recoverable error except the one LOSTSYNC at the guard. Homebrew installs measure macOS/Linux package demand for whole distributions (the mpg123 player and library; the mad formula library), not direct use of the decoding API. libmpg123 is the same engine counted under mp3_id3v2/c, and libmad is the decoder behind the SoX path there. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

cells.selection: Eight control-verified C++ JSON packages rank by comparable Debian source-package sourcemax installations: JsonCpp 32,707, simdjson 2,688, nlohmann/json 1,799, RapidJSON 899, Glaze 171, PicoJSON 16, jsoncons 3, and taoJSON 2. cells.uncertainty: Ten C++ JSON package paths pass two valid controls with scoped parser source coverage and stable AFL++ feedback. Glaze uses a generic_i64 DOM and a parser-only probe; POCO JSON reaches its ParserImpl and bundled pdjson tokenizer with a parser-only probe. jsoncons uses the insertion-ordered ojson tree and a parser-only probe whose AFL++ allowlist names the basic_json_parser methods, because a file-only allowlist dropped parser functions whose first instruction is inlined from another header; PicoJSON and taoJSON use the same function-scoped allowlist approach. PicoJSON and taoJSON store objects in std::map, so their trees lose source key order: their controls check array order and integer/float kinds exactly but compare object members by key. taoJSON runs its own grammar on the separately pinned PEGTL 3.2.6 engine, and its 1.0.0-beta.14 tag is an upstream pre-release; no final 1.0.0 exists. The lowest ranks rest on weak signals: PicoJSON 16 installations (0 recent), jsoncons 3 (1 recent), and taoJSON 2 (both no_files). Glaze has 171 comparable Debian source-package installations, but the source metric favors runtime packages and undercounts header-only libraries. Boost.JSON and POCO have no JSON-specific Debian source count and remain primary-unranked; POCO's 190 libpoco-dev installs are suite-wide, while its component runtime 125 are all classified no_files. One documentation lead remains unresolved: Qt. The 320 JSON-name source hits exclude Glaze, found by a supplementary exact source-name lookup. No complete top-ten claim follows. Two small valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259, numeric boundaries, other encodings, or malformed-input behavior.

cells.selection: JCodec (76), MP3SPI (55), JLayer (33), jaudiotagger (8) and mp3agic (6) have comparable summed deps.dev direct-dependent metrics and exact outputs on two valid untagged Layer III controls. The first three decode PCM; jaudiotagger verifies first-frame header fields, and mp3agic verifies header fields from its local-file scan. Each has own Java parser source-line coverage and stable parser-derived AFL++ feedback.
cells.family_note: JCodec and JLayer are independent decoders; MP3SPI delegates to a JLayer fork. jaudiotagger and mp3agic have their own MPEG header code, each already present as the same package in the tagged-MP3 cell; jid3lib shares historical ancestry with them.
cells.uncertainty: Five pure-Java Layer III paths verified; no padding. jaudiotagger is first-header-only and mp3agic reports only accurate header fields. Both higher-level APIs misidentify the valid 22.05 kHz control start at byte 104 and estimate 5 rather than 12 frames; mp3agic reports 261 ms versus oracle about 313 ms. These paths make no whole-file frame-count or duration claim. JavaMP3 1.0.1 decodes the mono control exactly but crashes on valid 22.05 kHz stereo input, so is excluded with a reproducible probe. Maven Central phrase queries returned no hits, so named leads were inspected via deps.dev and package documentation. deps.dev counts whole-package dependency use, not MP3-specific calls. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5 or ID3 behavior. Java SE 25 exports no MP3 reader by inventory.

Pilot cell: ten high-download package/API paths have valid nested-object and nested-array controls, package parser coverage, and AFL++ feedback; nine parser families are represented. jsonparse (105,362,611 downloads) has no API in its README; Parser.write(Buffer) is evidenced by packaged examples and tests. The adapter requires one root and checks the parser stack and tokenizer state. JSONStream (56,299,470 downloads) is a separate stream API path over the same pinned jsonparse 1.3.1 tokenizer, not an independent engine. JSONStream.parse([]) emits one root according to packaged code and tests despite its README statement. Its private parser exposes no end-of-input completeness check: the adapter requires one emitted root, no error, and stream end, but trailing unfinished syntax after a complete root may go undetected. JSONStream own package source is covered; differential feedback on the valid controls arises only in underlying jsonparse source. @humanwhocodes/momoa (18,038,222 downloads) has a documented string API only: the adapter decodes local bytes as strict UTF-8 and calls parse(text, {mode: 'json'}), which rejects tokens after the first value; the summary is taken from its AST nodes. @streamparser/json receives the entire Buffer and checks trailing bytes after the first root for whitespace. json5 is a JSON5 superset parser with its own lexer and state machine. It parses both valid strict JSON controls exactly through a documented text API, but accepts JSON5-only syntax and its high download count mainly reflects configuration-file use. json-bigint also has a documented string API: the adapter decodes local bytes strictly, then tags the parser's returned tree. Its Crockford-derived parser source is distinct from the other selected families; BigNumber behavior for long numeric tokens is not established by these controls. jsonc-parser adds a strict-option parseTree text API over its own Microsoft scanner/tree parser; both valid controls match but do not test JSONC extension rejection. lossless-json independently parses strict local UTF-8 text into type-tagged values whose numeric lexemes remain exact LosslessNumber strings; the two valid controls show parser-source coverage and stable input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Other high-download leads remain unresolved. Downloads cover 24 hand-picked candidates, not every search hit. Standard JSON.parse is separate. Two valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

Pilot cell with ten verified third-party paths: saxes 6.0.0, jsdom 31.0.1, sax 1.6.1, fast-xml-parser 5.12.1, @xmldom/xmldom 0.9.12, xml2js 0.6.2, xml-js 1.6.11, htmlparser2 12.0.0 xmlMode, xmldoc 3.0.0, and @xml-tools/parser 1.0.12 are control-verified, source-covered, and have input-dependent AFL++ feedback. Comparable 30-day npm downloads rank the ten package paths; counts include transitive adoption. The ten paths cover six independent parser families: jsdom shares saxes and xml2js shares sax. saxes and sax share historical fork lineage but have distinct parser code. fast-xml-parser has its own scanner and validator but no namespace URI resolution, so the adapter resolves expanded names over its qualified names and xmlns attributes. @xmldom/xmldom has its own XMLReader tokenizer and DOM builder, accepts locally decoded text, and the adapter treats every warning or error as fatal. jsdom builds its XML DOM over the same pinned saxes 6.0.0 tokenizer as the selected saxes path; it copies DOCTYPE entity declarations into saxes and forces XML 1.0 rules, and its AFL++ feedback includes input-independent window setup alongside saxes and DOM construction. xml2js, xml-js and xmldoc build distinct trees over the same pinned sax 1.6.1 tokenizer as the selected sax path; it drops comments and processing instructions, which can merge adjacent text segments. Wrapper package and underlying tokenizer source coverage are recorded separately. xmlbuilder2 4.0.3 is excluded from this namespace-aware selection: its native DOM misassigns the c:catalog and c:lang namespace URIs on the valid catalog control; the adapter does not repair them. htmlparser2 xmlMode has its own forgiving tokenizer but no XML well-formedness or namespace-URI enforcement; it is selected only as a raw-name XML event path, and its 526,964,241 downloads mostly measure HTML use. xmldoc builds a raw-name tree over sax; it omits prolog comments and PIs. Both are compared only to a non-namespace Expat oracle projected to preserved fields, without adapter-side namespace repair. @xml-tools/parser returns a raw-QName Chevrotain CST without namespace URI expansion or decoded entity text; the Expat raw-name hierarchy matches both controls, and parser ALT callback hit-count feedback changes on 11 ranges while ordinary covered-line sets do not. The search is bounded to recorded queries and snapshot; two valid controls do not establish complete XML 1.0 compliance.

cells.selection: mediabunny 1.66.0 (26,071,768 downloads), music-metadata 12.5.0 (9,827,896), codec-parser 2.5.0 (2,683,215), mp3-duration 1.1.0 (43,261), and mp3-parser 0.3.0 (40,519) are five verified JavaScript MPEG frame-reading paths. The first four expose frame-aware structure or metadata; mp3-duration exposes only frame-derived duration. Each parses both valid untagged controls against an independent header walker, has source coverage, and stable parser-scoped AFL++ feedback. None decodes Layer III audio.
cells.uncertainty: Five verified paths; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Download counts cover whole toolkits: mediabunny's muxing, conversion and many containers, and codec-parser's AAC, FLAC and Ogg parsers, not MP3 framing alone. The first three remain the highest-download fetched candidates; mp3-duration and mp3-parser have lower adoption. mp3-parser has 40,519 monthly downloads, below the duration-only leads, and is selected for its documented frame reader and exact whole-control walk. Its AFL++ differential is narrow: two source ranges in lib.js octetToBinRep bit extraction, not distinct version/channel branches. None decodes Layer III audio. The mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5, CRC-protected or ID3 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists. codec-parser's valid-control AFL++ differential is narrow: one header-cache range that tracks distinct frame headers, not version or channel branches. Its V8 line counts include module evaluation of imported AAC, FLAC, Opus, Vorbis and Ogg files that audio/mpeg parsing does not call. music-metadata reports MPEG version and layer only through its codec string ('MPEG 1 Layer 3'), not as separate fields, and needs duration: true for a full frame walk. Its valid-control AFL++ differential is 4 sync() tail-policy ranges that track frame length, not version or channel branches. Its V8 package line count (3,539) is mostly module evaluation; MpegParser.js alone is 245 lines. mp3-duration exposes only duration; its count-scoped AFL signal tracks 11 versus 12 frame calls and may reflect input length, not a new branch or line. The same release is also verified for tagged MP3 duration in the ID3v2 cell.
cells.family_note: mediabunny, music-metadata, codec-parser mp3-duration and mp3-parser are separate parser families: different authors, repositories and frame-sync code; codec-parser 2.5.0 has no runtime dependencies. music-metadata shares its parser family with the mp3_id3v2/javascript music-metadata path (12.4.0 there, verified for ID3v2 tags); this cell verifies its MpegParser on untagged frames. Neither mediabunny nor codec-parser is among the mp3_id3v2/javascript paths.

cells.uncertainty: Ten positive-signal Python JSON third-party paths pass valid nested object and array controls with source-level parser coverage and AFL++ feedback: pydantic 2.14.3 (1,139,429,690 PyPI Stats last-month downloads), jiter 0.19.0 (421,162,504), orjson 3.13.0 (218,014,317), json5 0.17.3 (50,036,028), simplejson 4.3.0 (49,365,386), ijson 3.6.0 (46,615,664), msgspec 0.22.0 (39,138,375), ujson 6.1.0 (29,543,889), python-rapidjson 1.26 (4,066,455), and pysimdjson 8.0.0 (679,340). Pydantic embeds Jiter 0.18.0; standalone jiter uses Jiter 0.19.0 through a distinct package API. These are shared-family paths, not independent parsers, and their package downloads are not combined; orjson shares the yyjson C syntax-parser family but this pilot measures its Rust deserializer, not vendored C source lines. ijson uses the asserted yajl2_c backend, with pinned YAJL C tokenizer and Python extension coverage; its source-built embedded YAJL -O0 route differs from the official Linux wheel linkage and optimisation, and its other backends are untested. msgspec uses its own C JSON decoder in _core.c through untyped msgspec.json.decode; its source-built clang -O0 path differs from the official GCC wheel, typed decoding is untested, and JSON decoder sections are counted separately from other codecs in the same file. ujson uses its own UltraJSON C decoder with vendored double-conversion C++ for fractional numbers; both controls equal an exact CPython json oracle tree, and duplicate-key and edge-number behavior is recorded from source, not tested. python-rapidjson parses a local BytesIO stream through rapidjson.load with vendored Tencent RapidJSON v1.1.0-763-g24b5e7a8, the same RapidJSON C++ family as the C++ RapidJSON path at a later revision; RapidJSON reader.h and the rapidjson.cpp wrapper are counted separately, and default number conversion bypasses RapidJSON strtod. PyPI package downloads include non-parse uses and transitive installs. json5 is a pure-Python JSON5 superset parser (glop-generated PEG parser.py plus lib.py conversion) that never calls the standard json module; json5.loads on bytes, on text and json5.load on a stream give the exact type-tagged CPython json oracle tree for both controls, with 668 covered package lines and stable feedback differing by 27 parser.py lines and 27 AFL++ tuples. It accepts JSON5-only syntax, so it does not reject non-RFC 8259 input, and its downloads mainly reflect JSON5 configuration use. The bounded PyPI Simple index search (six project-name queries, first 100 alphabetical hits each) and a top-15,000 download list used only as a discovery aid added 22 leads: json5 was promoted, 8 are excluded (pydantic-core is the same binary as the pydantic path; pandas, pyarrow and polars are tabular readers; srsly, partial-json-parser and commentjson delegate to ujson or CPython json; jsonnet evaluates a language) and 13 remain unresolved. Unresolved json-repair (43,691,294; own repair parser only with skip_json_loads=True, host probe matched both controls), dirtyjson and hjson (simplejson-derived), pyjson5 and json-stream have higher downloads than pysimdjson and some than python-rapidjson, so these ten are not a definitive top ten by the metric. pysimdjson uses vendored simdjson 5.1.1 DOM and a generated Cython wrapper; native parser and wrapper source lines are reported separately. Python standard json is separately verified.

search_queries: targeted PyPI and project-documentation lookups for nine named XML parsers
cells.uncertainty: Seven verified third-party paths (lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml, xmltodict, xmlschema, parsel and untangle) are selected from nine named PyPI/project-documentation leads. A bounded PyPI Simple Index search remains pending; 2 leads are unresolved, so this is not a completed top-ten ranking. lxml uses source-built libxml2 2.15.4; beautifulsoup4's documented 'xml' builder runs on the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared parser family, no independent XML tokenizer, recover=True); xmltodict, defusedxml (guarded pure-Python ElementTree XMLParser), untangle (SAX via defusedxml's DefusedExpatParser) and the standard ElementTree path use Expat. defusedxml is a guard facade over CPython ElementTree, not an independent XML engine; its own code is constant on the valid controls, and ElementTree keeps no xmlns declarations, so its comparison with the lxml oracle omits the declaration count. untangle runs SAX without namespace processing and drops namespace URIs; its controls are checked against an lxml oracle projected to untangle's qualified-name view, not against namespace-expanded names. The lxml, beautifulsoup4, defusedxml and untangle controls exercise valid UTF-8 XML 1.0 namespace structures without DOCTYPE, not full XML conformance. PyPI Stats package downloads are not XML-specific use; Beautiful Soup downloads are mostly HTML use, and defusedxml downloads are largely transitive. lxml, beautifulsoup4 and parsel AFL feedback excludes parser.c lines 8700-8720 because address-sensitive attribute hash lookups varied across identical valid replays. xmlschema's XMLResource is not an independent XML engine: it consumes CPython's default xml.etree.ElementTree.iterparse events over the C _elementtree parser, pyexpat and Expat 2.10.0. It records xmlns declarations and per-element namespace maps itself, so its controls match the lxml path's full summary including the declaration count; its own 110 lines are the same on both controls and only their hit counts differ. xmlschema downloads are mostly XSD validation use. parsel's documented Selector(body=bytes, type='xml') is not an independent XML tokenizer: it strips the body and NUL bytes and calls lxml.etree.fromstring with SafeXMLParser(recover=True, resolve_entities=False, huge_tree=True) over the same lxml 6.1.3/libxml2 2.15.4 pins (shared lxml/libxml2 family). Both valid controls match an independent CPython pyexpat oracle. Parsel's own 100 selector.py lines are the same on both controls, so its input-dependent AFL++ feedback (209 tuples) comes entirely from libxml2 parser.c. Parsel downloads are mostly Scrapy HTML scraping use.

cells.selection: mutagen (10,748,990), tinytag (4,453,166) and hachoir (222,718) are the three most-downloaded candidates whose own Python source parses MPEG Layer III frame headers from a documented byte or file-object API. av, soundfile, pydub and librosa rank higher but hand frame parsing to native FFmpeg or libsndfile/libmpg123, or to an external ffmpeg process; audioread (7,283,376) ranks between mutagen and tinytag and dispatches to native backends; pygame, pymediainfo and miniaudio rank between tinytag and hachoir and wrap native decoders.
cells.shared_family: Same Mutagen package, release 1.48.1 and mutagen/mp3 module as the mp3_id3v2/python mutagen entry. This cell checks MPEGInfo on untagged streams; it is not an independent parser family. tinytag is an independent pure-Python family (its _MPEG class in tinytag/tinytag.py). hachoir is a third independent pure-Python family (hachoir/parser/audio/mpeg_audio.py on hachoir's own field/stream framework).
cells.uncertainty: Three verified paths; no padding. The name search is a substring filter over the PyPI Simple index (serial 43764887) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' and 'mpeg' hit lists were not triaged one by one, and download numbers were fetched only for 13 named candidates, so a less obvious frame parser could be missed. Native wrappers (av, soundfile, audioread, pygame, pymediainfo, miniaudio) are unresolved, not rejected: their parsers are real but outside Python source coverage. eyed3 and pymp3 are unresolved pure-Python leads. Mutagen reads headers and checks frame syncs but does not decode audio; for CBR streams without Xing/Info/VBRI its duration is stream bytes divided by the first header's bitrate. TinyTag also only reads headers: after five equal-bitrate frames it estimates duration from stream size and mean frame length, and it does not expose MPEG version, layer or frame count. Both full-length controls run the same TinyTag lines; its feedback difference is shown with a valid three-frame prefix of the 44.1 kHz control. hachoir is called through its MpegAudioFile class directly, not guessParser, whose fallback tries every hachoir parser in set order. It walks every frame header to EOF and reports version, layer, sample rate, bitrate, channel mode and frame count. It does not decode audio or side information, and its two controls differ by only 4 mpeg_audio.py lines: the MPEG-1 versus MPEG-2 bitrate table and frame-length formula. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.

Ten verified Rust JSON parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (600 hits, 476 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Ten documented leads remain unverified, so this is a bounded pilot rather than a complete top-ten ranking. ijson 0.1.7 was excluded after source inspection: it has an IValue type deserialized through serde_json::from_slice and no own local JSON parser API. Downloads are 90-day adoption proxies that include transitive pulls. Two small valid controls establish only observed RFC 8259 structure; duplicate keys, huge numbers, deep nesting and non-UTF-8 are untested.

Nine verified XML parser paths selected within the first 100 hits of seven crates.io queries (642 hits, 483 unique), captured 2026-11-17. Seven documented leads remain unverified. xml5ever 0.40.0 is an XML5 error-recovering superset parser: the two valid XML 1.0 controls verify namespace-aware output, but it does not establish strict XML 1.0 well-formedness, complete namespace behavior, DTD support, or other encodings. rxml 0.14.0 is a deliberately restricted XML 1.0 parser without DTDs, custom entities or processing instructions, and it rejects comments by default. It parses the shared catalog control exactly but rejects the shared order control (Error(RestrictedXml("comments"))), so its second control is order-default-ns-restricted.xml without that comment and processing instruction. The xml-rs 1.0.0 package is a compatibility re-export of xml and excluded as a duplicate family. minidom 0.19.0 is a DOM wrapper over the selected rxml family: rxml's RawReader lexes and parses, and minidom's own TreeBuilder resolves prefixes and builds the tree. It inherits rxml's restricted subset, so it also rejects the shared order control and uses the restricted order control; its stable AFL++ edge differential has no change in minidom source-line counts, and the differing lines are in rxml. uppsala 0.12.1 parses both shared valid controls through its own namespace-aware DOM parser; the controls do not establish its XPath, XSD or XSLT features, DTD handling, other encodings, or complete XML 1.0 conformance. Downloads include transitive pulls and are adoption proxies; ranks compare selected paths only, and the minidom and rxml counts overlap because minidom depends on rxml. RustyXML 0.3.0 parses both shared valid controls through its own ObjFW-derived streaming parser; its README lists incomplete error checking, so the controls do not establish strict XML 1.0 well-formedness checking, DTD handling or non-UTF-8 encodings. Its AFL++ overlay fixes std HashMap RandomState keys with a getrandom AFL_PRELOAD shim; see data/rust/xml/rustyxml-feedback-audit.md.

Six verified package paths cover four parser families on two valid untagged CBR controls: Symphonia's Rust MP3 demuxer/decoder, reached directly through symphonia-bundle-mp3 and through the symphonia facade's probe and codec registry; minimp3's C decoder through the Rust minimp3 binding and as the pure-Rust nanomp3 port; the mp3-duration frame-header scanner, which reports only a summed duration; rusty_mp3's in-house pure-Rust Layer III decoder. The symphonia facade is a separate package API over the same Symphonia family, not a new engine; nanomp3 is a separate package API over the minimp3 family (its minimp3-compatible PCM is byte-identical to scalar minimp3.h), and nanomp3-core, the decoder it re-exports, is counted only through nanomp3. Five leads remain unresolved, so the verified ranks are not a claim about all MP3 parsers. Search covers the first 100 hits of six crates.io queries (591 hits, 350 unique) captured 2026-11-17; the 'mp3' query alone reports 1119 matches. Recent downloads include transitive dependency pulls and are an adoption proxy, not evidence of direct MP3 parsing use. The two controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II or MPEG-2.5 support.

Laminas, JSON Machine, salsify and pcrov also passed a valid nested array control and stable source-line AFL feedback. Laminas is abandoned, and its own decoder runs only when explicitly enabled; its default API route delegates to ext/json. JSON Machine shares ext/json for member decoding. salsify accepts only object/array roots and silently accepts concatenated documents, so its harness rejects anything other than one complete document; the tree-building listener is harness code. Two own-parser or partial-own-parser leads remain unverified; five json_decode wrappers are excluded, including colinodell/json5 on both valid controls. pcrov/jsonreader has a separate lexer and state machine, with three parser-source features and AFL tuples differing between the valid controls. The bounded search used five Packagist queries of at most 100 hits each. Package downloads measure overall/historical adoption, not JSON parsing frequency. Valid controls do not establish complete RFC 8259 support.

cells.uncertainty: Pilot cell, six verified third-party paths. The earlier zero count wrongly excluded libxml2-family wrappers; PROTOCOL.md lets a wrapper qualify as a package API with its parser family identified, so sabre/xml is counted with family libxml2 (shared with the standard XMLReader path). symfony/dom-crawler was reassessed under the same wrapper rule and counted: its package-own scope is Crawler navigation and XPath/namespace mapping over a libxml2 DOMDocument, not tokenizing, and its Xdebug package lines differ by only one post-parse line between the two controls, so its AFL++ feedback comes from a native overlay (source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4, allowlist limited to libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c and ext/dom document.c plus ext/libxml) running the same Crawler harness, where the controls differ in 357 stable tuples, all arising while addXmlContent parses; its downloads are mostly HTML crawling uses. jms/serializer stays excluded because it maps an already parsed SimpleXML tree onto a target class model. symfony/serializer maps a DOMDocument through XmlEncoder::decode; its Xdebug package lines are separate from 359 stable native parser-time AFL tuples, and its whole-component downloads mostly reflect other encoders. It drops the root name and descendant namespace declarations. veewee/xml preserves qualified names and per-element xmlns declarations but groups siblings; mtownsend/xml-to-array loses namespace URIs, declarations and attribute prefixes. Both have package-owned array mapping and parser-only native libxml2 AFL feedback, not new tokenizer families. prewk/xml-string-streamer is excluded after a pinned two-control probe showed raw byte slicing only. laravie/parser stays unresolved because Reader::load delegates to SimpleXML and Document::parse requires a caller schema, similar to excluded jms/serializer. saloonphp/xml-wrangler parses twice through veewee XMLReader and DOMDocument; its raw-name Element DTO loses namespace URI resolution and the nested empty-default undeclaration on the valid order control. Its 414 stable native AFL tuples are parser-derived, while package-own Xdebug lines are separate. The other libxml2-family wrappers (veewee/xml, mtownsend/xml-to-array, saloonphp/xml-wrangler, laravie/parser, orchestra/parser, pear/xml_parser and smaller ones) were not evaluated by the cutoff and remain unresolved, as do the own-code leads prewk/xml-string-streamer and watoki/dom. sabre/xml drops xmlns declarations and text in mixed-content elements by design, so its summary omits namespace declaration counts. Both coverage images use Ubuntu PHP 8.5.4 with libxml 2.15.2; both AFL++ overlays use the source-built PHP 8.5.12 and libxml2 2.15.4. The search covers the first 100 hits of five Packagist queries; controls are two small UTF-8 namespace-aware documents without DOCTYPE. Standard paths: XMLReader::XML, DOMDocument::loadXML, simplexml_load_string and xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse are four PHP 8.5.12 runtime APIs over the same source-built libxml2 2.15.4, counted separately from the third-party paths and not ranked; DOMDocument::loadXML and simplexml_load_string take the control as an in-memory string, and their AFL++ overlays instrument only libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/dom document.c or ext/simplexml simplexml.c. SimpleXML exposes no separate text nodes, so its summary merges mixed-content character data per element (neither control has any); simplexml.c also holds the traversal methods, which the parse-only fuzz target does not call. xml_parser_create_ns/xml_parse is the only push-parser entry point (xmlCreatePushParserCtxt/xmlParseChunk through ext/xml/compat.c's expat-style SAX callbacks, no tree); its summary comes from event handlers with case folding off and a "\x01" namespace separator, the controls go in one final chunk, and its AFL++ overlay instruments libxml2 parser.c/parserInternals.c/SAX2.c plus ext/xml xml.c and compat.c. ext/xml has no comment handler (comments reach the default handler) and reports user-defined entity references unexpanded to the default handler, which the harness rejects.

cells.selection: james-heinrich/getid3 (15,766,894 Packagist downloads) and wapmorgan/mp3info (1,512,916) are the two highest-download hits whose native PHP code reads MPEG Layer III frame headers from untagged input. getID3's module.audio.mp3.php matches both controls. Mp3Info 0.1.1 matches the MPEG-1 control's version, layer, sample rate, channel mode, bitrate, audio bytes and 11-frame count against the header-walk oracle, but misreads the MPEG-2 control; its scope is MPEG-1 Layer III CBR.
cells.shared_family: getID3 is the same code base already counted in the active mp3_id3v2/php cell (james-heinrich/getid3 v1.9.28 and its wrappers). This pilot covers a different module (module.audio.mp3.php frame headers, 273 lines covered on the control) of the same family, not an independent parser. Mp3Info is a separate family: one class (src/Mp3Info.php) with its own tables and no getID3 code; its ID3v2 reader is counted in mp3_id3v2/php and wapmorgan/media-file wraps it.
cells.uncertainty: Two verified paths; no padding. Search is seven Packagist search.json queries capped at 50 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; package descriptions alone decided most exclusions. Packagist total downloads count Composer installs of the whole package (and wrappers pull getID3 or Mp3Info transitively), not use of the MPEG frame parser. getID3 reads the first frame header, checks sync on following frames, and derives CBR duration from audio-data bytes and the header bitrate. Mp3Info reads two headers, estimates frames from audio bytes and the computed frame length, and reports duration one frame short ((frames - 1) x 1152 / sample rate). On the MPEG-2 control it uses the MPEG-1 frame-length coefficient, misses the third frame and reads a false sync at byte 236, reporting Layer II 24 kHz mono 96 kbit/s; MPEG-2 is not covered for Mp3Info. Neither path decodes audio. PHP-MP3 (falahati/php-mp3) failed the controls: the v0.9.5-alpha2 tag does not return on PHP 8.5, and the dev-master snapshot reads the MPEG-2 control as 3 frames at 11,025 Hz (data/php/mp3/falahati-php-mp3-control-audit.md). The Zend media reader and fobilow/mp3file are unresolved independent candidates. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, or MPEG-2.5 support.
